And the reading material in the German class is again related to Soviet experiences and moral values Grade 5 “The Common Viper” (Die Kreuzotter) , Yury Sotnik Categorize the people on the train into: Borja’s supporters, Borja’s opponents, and those who fluctuate. “The Fireman of Train No. 71” , Alexander Kononov “Three-Quarters of a Hundred Short Stories” , Erwin Strittmatter A few quick notes on the literary titles: “Flämmchen” : Literally means “Little Flame”. Since it functions as a proper name/character in the book, keeping it in German or using “Little Flame” both work well depending on your target audience. “Ede und Unku” : This is a very well-known classic of German children’s literature (about the friendship between a Berlin boy and a Sinti girl during the Weimar Republic). The names are proper nouns, so they remain unchanged. “Die Kreuzotter” : Literally the European adder or common viper.
